why: MCP tool schemas are not lazy. A skill costs nothing until its description matches; a connected MCP server puts every one of its tool schemas into the model's context on every turn, in every session, whether or not the task is related. Measured in this pack: 146 skill bodies are far larger than the description index an agent actually reads. There is no equivalent discount for MCP. So the servers here are NOT registered globally: every profile below is project-scoped, wired only for the one project whose markers asked for it, and only when the machine can actually run it. Decided by TOOLS/Set-McpProfile.ps1 from the markers in 'detect' and the preconditions in 'requires'.
always_on_note: The always-on core is context7, github, and headroom, in TOOLS/Add-Reasoning-MCPs.ps1, not here. They earn permanent slots for current documentation, verified repository state, and context inspection/compression. sequential-thinking is the opt-in reasoning profile after measurement showed its permanent schema cost. Playwright is in the web profile; Firecrawl and Perplexity register only when their keys exist.

requires_forms.command: A command that must resolve on PATH, or an absolute path that must exist as a file.
requires_forms.any_path: At least one of these paths must exist. Entries may contain environment variables and a single '*' wildcard per segment.
requires_forms.env: This environment variable must be set and non-empty. Used for servers that cannot do anything without a key.
requires_forms.project_rel: A path relative to the project directory that must exist. Project-scoped servers only.
requires_forms.auto_install: Steps this pack may run unattended to satisfy the requirement, when 'requires_command' resolves. Package installs only -- never something that needs a GUI, a licence acceptance, or a credential. An auto_install makes a tool INSTALLED, never ENABLED: registration is still decided per project.

profiles.title: Repository graph plus language-server-accurate navigation and editing
profiles.why: Serena drives real language servers, so find-symbol, find-referencing-symbols and replace-symbol-body answer from the compiler's view of the code rather than from a text match. It overlaps codebase-memory-mcp deliberately: that one answers 'where is this in the graph', Serena answers 'what exactly does this symbol resolve to, and rewrite its body'. Worth the context on a real codebase, not worth it on a two-file mod -- which is why it is wired for that codebase and nowhere else. Named code-intel, not code-deep: it was renamed in 7.9.6 and has nothing to do with any package of a similar name.

servers.note: persistent code graph for repository structure and relationships
LSP-accurate symbol search and symbol-level editing (Serena)
servers.install_hint: uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent && serena init
servers.upstream_setup: serena setup {claude-code|codex|grok} registers Serena machine-wide for that client. This pack deliberately does not call it: a machine-wide registration is the cost this file exists to avoid.
servers.context_note: --context trims the tool set to what the client does not already have. Serena 1.7.0 ships named contexts for claude-code, codex and grok; Kimi and Hermes have none, so they get the generic 'agent' context. --project pins the registration to the project it was written for; --project-from-cwd is used instead for a -Global registration, since one baked path would activate the wrong project everywhere else. --enable-web-dashboard false keeps Serena from opening a browser window and from leaving an HTTP listener on the machine. Upstream recommends leaving the dashboard on and setting --open-web-dashboard false instead; this pack does not start a local web server a user did not ask for, and uses TOOLS/Test-McpHandshake.ps1 for diagnosis.

auto_install.why: Serena is a Python tool, not an npx package, so it has to exist on disk before a config can point at it. uv installs it into an isolated environment with its own interpreter.

servers.side_effect_note: Activating a project makes Serena write .serena/project.yml inside it on first run. That happens only for a project the profile was explicitly enabled for.

profiles.title: Live browser inspection and debugging
profiles.why: Chrome DevTools MCP reads a real Chrome: console messages, network requests, performance traces and the rendered DOM. That is the half playwright-mcp does not do -- playwright drives a browser, this one explains what the browser did. Enable it for front-end work; it is dead weight in a Papyrus session.

servers.note: drive a browser for testing and automation
servers.requires_note: Claude is excluded because it already has a browser pane. Set PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH before enabling to use Opera GX, Edge, Brave, or Vivaldi instead of the default Chrome channel.

servers.note: console, network, performance traces and DOM from a live Chrome
servers.requires_note: Upstream supports Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only. Chromium forks (Edge, Brave, Opera GX, Vivaldi) are not supported by this server; playwright-mcp is the one that takes PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH.
servers.flag_note: --no-usage-statistics opts out of Google's telemetry for this server. It is on by default upstream, and this pack does not enable third-party telemetry on a user's machine without asking.

servers.note: search, inspect and add components from configured shadcn registries
servers.requires_note: The server resolves registries from the project's components.json, so it is meaningless outside a shadcn project and is written project-scoped only.

profiles.title: Skyrim mod engineering (Skyrim Forge)
profiles.why: Skyrim Forge exposes a large typed tool surface for plugins, Papyrus, frameworks, assets, packaging and release gates. Keep the product and skill installed everywhere, but connect its MCP only inside a Skyrim mod project; providers without project-scoped MCP config use the same Forge CLI through the skyrim-forge skill.

servers.note: typed Skyrim mod engineering and release gates

profiles.title: Skyrim installed load order (houseCARL)
profiles.why: houseCARL is useful against a real MO2 instance or the bundle's Vortex shim, not in every Skyrim source repository. Its broad load-order and patching schemas activate only when the opened directory is an actual manager instance/shim.

servers.note: inspect and patch the active Skyrim load order

profiles.title: Roblox project engineering (Roblox Forge)
profiles.why: Roblox Forge's eleven tools are useful for a Roblox filesystem project and waste schema context elsewhere. The bundle discovers an existing official checkout and activates it only for Rojo, Rokit, place, or model markers.

servers.note: Roblox project analysis, planning, review and receipts

profiles.title: Saints Row mod engineering (Saints Row Forge)
profiles.why: Saints Row Forge is a game-specific local server. Its MCP activates only when project.json identifies a supported Saints Row game or when a top-level game asset marker exists; other sessions keep using zero schemas from it.

servers.note: Saints Row assets, XTBL, projects, builds and dependency checks

profiles.title: Blender scene control
profiles.why: Inspect and drive a running Blender: objects, materials, modifiers, and Python execution in the live scene. Relevant to this pack because Skyrim mesh work rides on Blender.

servers.note: live Blender scene inspection and control
servers.editor_side_note: The server talks to an addon inside Blender. `install-addon` copies it into the user addons folder, but ENABLING it is inside the editor process and cannot be done from outside -- so Set-McpProfile prints the command rather than pretending it ran it. 'The MCP executable starts' and 'the addon is connected' are different claims: the server answers initialize with no Blender running at all. Only a tool call that reaches the scene proves the second.
servers.requires_note: Discovered, never hardcoded. 7.9.6 listed a Steam path on this maintainer's own drive letter, which could not match on anybody else's machine -- the exact class of path this pack forbids elsewhere. The first two entries are what `uvx blender-mcp@1.8.3 addon-paths` reports: Blender creates that user directory on first run whatever the install source, Steam included.
servers.telemetry_note: There is no telemetry flag to pass this server. Read from the 1.8.3 wheel: the bundled addon carries a `telemetry_consent` preference and attaches its edit-capture handlers only with consent, and the addon contains no telemetry endpoint (its outbound URLs are PolyHaven, Rodin and Sketchfab, each separately toggled in the addon). So it is off unless you turn it on, inside Blender's addon preferences, where this pack cannot reach it. Stated rather than claimed: nothing here disabled anything.

profiles.title: Godot project control
profiles.why: Run a Godot project, read its scene tree and capture runtime errors without leaving the agent loop.

servers.note: run Godot projects, read scene trees, capture runtime errors
servers.requires_note: The server shells out to the Godot editor binary and cannot find it by itself on Windows, where Godot has no fixed install location. Gated on GODOT_PATH rather than registered as a server that fails on first call: setx GODOT_PATH "C:\path\to\Godot.exe".
servers.alternative_evaluated: hi-godot/godot-ai, compared 2026-08-21 on capability / context cost / setup friction / reliability. It is the fresher project (last push 2026-08-21 against Coding-Solo/godot-mcp 2026-04-16) but has fewer stars (1,822 against 5,299), is not published on npm under that name, and requires installing a Godot EDITOR PLUGIN which then starts the server itself and connects over WebSocket -- plus uv as a second runtime. That is the Unity-MCP shape: an editor-side step this pack cannot automate and must print. Coding-Solo runs headless through the Godot binary via a pinned npx package and one environment variable, which is the lower-friction fit for a bundle whose Godot support is incidental. Kept. Revisit if Coding-Solo goes a year without a push, or if a user needs live editor integration rather than run-and-read-the-scene-tree.

profiles.title: Unity editor control
profiles.why: Read and drive an open Unity project -- GameObjects, components, assets, console, play mode.

servers.note: live Unity editor control (per-project server binary)
servers.requires_note: Unity-MCP does not ship a machine-wide server. The executable is generated inside the project's Library folder by the Unity package, so there is no global registration to write -- the entry is project-scoped by construction, and the command is the resolved absolute path for that one project. Until the package is installed the exe does not exist, and the profile refuses rather than writing a path that is not there.

profiles.title: Explicit step-by-step decomposition (sequential-thinking)
profiles.why: Held an always-on slot through 7.9.6 and lost it on measurement in 7.9.7: one tool, but a 4,587-byte schema -- ~1,146 tokens on every turn of every session, as much as context7's two tools. It is a structured scratchpad, not a capability: it fetches nothing and reaches nothing the model could not write in its own reasoning, while this pack ships decomposition skills that cost nothing until they match and every provider it targets has native reasoning. Kept as an opt-in rather than deleted, because the benefit to WEAKER models was never benchmarked -- only the cost was. Turn it on with -Enable reasoning -Global if your provider has no native reasoning and you want it everywhere.
profiles.detect_note: Deliberately empty. This is a way of thinking, not a property of a project, so there is no marker that could honestly imply it. -Auto will never enable it.

servers.note: explicit step-by-step decomposition (~1,146 tokens per turn while enabled)

measured_cost.method: real MCP initialize -> tools/list over stdio, tools array serialized compactly

profiles.title: Windows desktop control through UI Automation (windows-mcp)
profiles.why: Every other capability here stops at a file or a browser tab. This one drives the machine: clicking, typing, shortcuts, PowerShell, the registry, the filesystem, windows and processes. It is the only way an agent in this pack can operate a native application, and UI Automation means it can read controls without spending a vision call on a screenshot. It costs ~5,522 tokens on every turn while enabled (20 tools, 22,088 bytes, measured 2026-08-27), which is cheap for the surface and still far too much to carry when you are not using it -- hence off by default, like everything else in this file. Global scope rather than project: a desktop is not a property of a repository, so there is no project this could honestly be scoped to. That is the same reasoning `reasoning` uses, and it means every session on the machine pays while it is on. Turn it off when you are done.
profiles.detect_note: Deliberately empty, and for a stronger reason than `reasoning`'s. That one is empty because a way of thinking is not a property of a directory. This one is empty because the profile can click, type, run PowerShell and write the registry, and no marker on disk is evidence that an operator wants an agent doing those things. -Auto will never enable it; -Enable windows -Global is the only way in.

servers.note: desktop control: click, type, shortcuts, PowerShell, registry, filesystem, windows, processes (~5,522 tokens per turn while enabled)

measured_cost.method: real MCP initialize -> tools/list over stdio, tools array serialized compactly, via TOOLS/Measure-McpSchemaCost.ps1

evaluated_not_shipped.reason: Last upstream commit 2025-06-06 and 113 stars at evaluation time. A bridge into a running editor is exactly the kind of component that breaks on an engine point release, and this pack pins exact versions precisely so it can tell when upstream has moved. Vendoring a bridge nobody is maintaining would ship that risk under a version number that implies otherwise.
No first-party server from the Storybook project at evaluation time. Community servers exist; none had provenance this pack would accept for an install it performs on a user's machine unattended.

Shipped as the 'cloud' profile in 7.9.5 and 7.9.6; removed in 7.9.7 at the owner's decision. It was also the only profile here that required an account and a personal access token, against this pack's default of free, local, keyless and no signup. Deliberately not replaced with another account-dependent backend MCP. Anyone who wants it can register @supabase/mcp-server-supabase themselves; the migration removes only entries this pack created and leaves an independently configured one alone.

evaluated_not_shipped.source: Cloudflare Browser Run (hosted, not a repository)
evaluated_not_shipped.reason: A browser built for agents, running on Cloudflare Workers. The headline figure is real -- Cloudflare's own numbers are 3.1-3.8x less CPU and 4.7-7x less memory than Chromium -- but the same measurement says tasks take 1.7-1.8x LONGER, which the recommendation that reached this pack had dropped. It is also account-gated, and an account requirement is the one thing test_bundle_stays_free_and_accountless exists to refuse: that contract was written when Supabase was withdrawn in 7.9.7 and it forbids any profile server carrying a key. Local playwright-mcp stays the browser.

Scans skills and MCP configs for dangerous patterns and baseline-hashes configs to catch a rug-pull. The IDEA is right and this pack is most of the way to it already -- MANIFEST hashing, RETIRED-SKILLS.json, RETIRED-PLUGINS.json and an installed-state doctor. The instance is the problem. Checked 2026-08-27: last commit 2026-06-11, latest PUBLISHED release v0.8.0 from 2026-03-25 while the tree carries an unreleased 0.10.0 bump, and GitHub detects no OSI license (NOASSERTION). It is also from the same owner as CodeBurn, which this pack already ships and which committed twice in the last three days -- the security tool is the quiet side of that org, not its focus. A config-hash baseline belongs in Test-Installed-State.ps1, where it runs on this pack's own cadence and depends on nothing.

installed_vs_enabled: Two different things, and conflating them is what made 7.9.5's code-deep expensive. INSTALLED means the executable exists on disk: it costs disk and nothing else, no model context, no startup time. ENABLED means an MCP entry is registered in a provider config, so the server is spawned and its tool schemas ride in context on every turn of every session that config covers. Set-McpProfile.ps1 will install a missing tool when it can (see auto_install) and still leave it disabled everywhere except the project that asked.

scope_forms.project: The default and, for every server in this file, the correct one. The entry is written where only sessions opened in that project can see it. What that means per provider is under provider_project_scope.
scope_forms.global: Written into the provider's machine-wide config, where every session pays for it. One profile declares it: 'reasoning' is a thinking aid rather than a project capability, so a project scope would be meaningless. It has no detection markers, so -Auto never turns it on; -Enable reasoning -Global is deliberate. Everything else here is project-scoped, and TOOLS/Set-McpProfile.ps1 -Global is the per-run override.

provider_project_scope.Claude: projects["<absolute project path>"].mcpServers in %USERPROFILE%\.claude.json -- the same place `claude mcp add --scope local` writes (verified against Claude Code 2.1.237). Chosen over the project's .mcp.json because it adds no file to the user's repository and raises no trust prompt. A team that wants the server checked in should copy the entry into .mcp.json by hand.
provider_project_scope.Grok: <project>\.grok\config.toml, the `project` scope of `grok mcp add -s project` (verified against grok 1.0.5). This one IS a file inside the project, because it is the only project mechanism grok-cli has.
provider_project_scope.Codex: None. `codex mcp add` has no scope flag and a project-local .codex/config.toml is ignored -- verified against codex-cli 0.147.0 by putting one there and reading `codex mcp list`. Capability servers are therefore not written for Codex unless -Global is passed.
provider_project_scope.Kimi: None found. kimi-code reads %USERPROFILE%\.kimi-code\mcp.json; a project-local .kimi-code\mcp.json was not picked up by `kimi doctor`. Not written unless -Global.
provider_project_scope.Hermes: Hermes has native named profiles, each with its own home/config, but no project-path MCP scope. TOOLS/Migrate-HermesProfiles.ps1 owns the default/roblox/skyrim topology; this path-based router skips Hermes unless -Global is explicit.

arg_forms.args_by_provider: Replaces args entirely for the named provider.
arg_forms.project_args: Appended when the entry is written project-scoped, where the project path is known.
arg_forms.global_args: Appended instead when the entry is written machine-wide with -Global. A server that needs to know its project must discover it from the session here, because one baked path would be wrong in every other session.
